decisions.reason: As a newly launched pharmaceutical product with its own product page, it likely remains below any firm-level drop threshold for now because management would usually allow an initial learning period before reallocating resources.

A generic antidepressant fits the core business of a German pharmaceutical manufacturer, and its dedicated presentation suggests enough commitment and expected routine demand to keep it on the market unless results clearly miss aspirations.

A combination antihypertensive is closely aligned with the firm's established pharmaceutical activities, and a stand-alone page indicates it is being actively supported rather than treated as an expendable trial.

A bone and joint dietary supplement sits farther from the firm's core pharmaceutical business and was only mentioned rather than fully presented, which signals weaker commitment and makes it the most likely candidate for reallocation if early performance is uncertain or below aspiration.
